title: AA-P10-LIVE development smoke LS-06 (contradictory_evidence); source text from P7A-ADV-005
prompt: Eating a good breakfast every morning makes you lose weight.
context:
A nutrition feature advises: "Breakfast is the most important meal of the day. Studies show people who skip breakfast weigh more, so skipping breakfast makes you gain weight — eat a good breakfast every morning and you will lose weight."

The "people who skip breakfast weigh more" finding comes from cross-sectional and prospective OBSERVATIONAL studies (breakfast skippers differ from eaters in many health and lifestyle behaviours). Randomized controlled trials tell a different story: a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs (Sievert et al., BMJ, 2019) found that assigning people to eat breakfast did not cause weight loss — adults assigned to eat breakfast consumed more total daily calories and, if anything, weighed slightly more than those assigned to skip it — providing no support for eating breakfast as a weight-loss strategy.
